answer: Each claim must set a pearl adrift on an ocean whose current is set by the last close hash, wandering a path only its own verified jobs could chart. Three peers read the drift trail against the ledger: a pearl from a copied chart sails dead straight and is beached, so the claim drops with its 105 POA fee burned. Each claim from one operator dives one fathom deeper, and the pressure fee follows the Fibonacci depth, so the Nth dive pays Fib(N) x 105 POA and 10 clones pay 15,015 POA. One pearl rides one tide for one identity and cannot be restrung across clones.
